```csharp
builder.Services.AddOptions<JwtOptions>()
    .BindConfiguration("Jwt")
    .Validate(options => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.Key) && options.Key.Length >= 32 && options.ExpirationMinutes > 0,

    .ValidateOnStart();
```

When frontend code is in scope, check against `.claude/rules/frontend/` (feature boundaries, data-access boundary, subscription lifetime, error contract, route guards not treated as server authorization, no unnecessary global state, meaningful tests). Do not build test infrastructure without a concrete testing need; a small project does not need an enterprise-sized harness.

Keep test data explicit and minimal. Introduce builders, fixtures, or factories when repeated setup becomes hard to read; do not add a generic test-data framework for a few simple objects.

"Smoke test" means a small set of fast checks that a built or deployed application is basically operational — not a synonym for every integration test. Coverage is diagnostic, not a target; prioritize meaningful behavior, edge cases, and risky integrations. Named, typed, and keyed clients are all valid; choose the model that makes ownership and lifetime easiest to understand.
- **Named** — a factory creates clients dynamically, several clients share a usage model, or a singleton creates clients per operation (`services.AddHttpClient("catalog", ...)`).
- **Keyed** — when keyed DI makes consumption clearer; not automatically because the framework supports it.

context_quotes:
- Default for new C# code: file-scoped namespaces when consistent with the project; one primary top-level type per file with a matching file name (small private or nested supporting types may stay with their owner); the `Async` suffix on `Task`/`ValueTask`-returning methods unless an existing or framework contract makes it inappropriate.
- Must not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.

- [ ] The selected package/version is not deprecated.
- [ ] Known vulnerability information from the ecosystem has been checked (`dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive`, `npm audit`, registry advisories). Scanner output needs context; do not upgrade or replace unrelated packages because of a finding.
- [ ] The license of the exact selected version is verified from official registry metadata (and the upstream license when necessary). Permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD-family licenses may normally be accepted; free download does not imply an acceptable license.

Remove dependencies that are no longer used when doing so is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead package references behind, and do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task.

Restore the affected scope to a green build/test state without hiding failures, weakening behavior, or introducing unrelated changes. `build-fix` repairs an existing failure; `code-review` inspects completed changes; `verify` proves a completed change is ready.
- Must not weaken, delete, skip, or suppress relevant tests, compiler, TypeScript, lint, or analyzer failures merely to make verification pass; understand a diagnostic before changing how it is reported.
- Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing; a green build obtained by violating them is not a successful repair.
- Stop when progress has clearly stalled instead of making speculative edits.

Determine which contract is authoritative (response shape, generated client vs. OpenAPI, enum/value semantics, endpoint path or method, nullability, authentication contract). Never patch both sides independently into inconsistent shapes merely to compile. With OpenAPI client generation: verify the backend contract, regenerate the client through the project's normal workflow, review the generated changes, then fix handwritten frontend code. Technique: `swagger`, `http-api`.

When the build succeeds but tests fail: read the failing test and the relevant production behavior; decide whether the defect lies in production code, test setup, the test expectation, environment/configuration, or an intentionally changed contract; make the smallest correct change; rerun the affected test, then broader relevant tests. Never turn a strong assertion into a weak one, and never delete or skip a failing test because fixing it is inconvenient. If expected behavior intentionally changed, update the test to express the new contract and confirm the change was actually requested.

For upgrade fallout, inspect the installed version, separate compile errors from changed runtime behavior, update obsolete APIs deliberately from verified documentation (never fabricate replacement APIs from memory), and do not perform an additional unrelated upgrade. For toolchain problems check `dotnet --info`, `dotnet --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`, `global.json`, target frameworks, frontend package versions, `package-lock.json`, and CI runtime versions. Never change the repository's declared SDK, Node, framework, or language version merely because the local machine differs; if the required toolchain is unavailable, report the limitation instead of editing source code to compensate.

Use bounded iteration — several focused attempts, not an unlimited edit/build loop. Stop and reassess when the same root failure survives materially different fixes, fixes create increasing unrelated failures, the toolchain is incompatible, required external infrastructure is unavailable, package compatibility cannot be resolved safely, or correct behavior cannot be determined. Never repeat variants of the same failed guess. If a fix introduces new failures, determine whether they reveal a legitimate dependency of the change; otherwise revert or correct the fix. Never leave the repository knowingly worse than where the repair started, and do not clean up unrelated pre-existing failures unless they block verification or the user asks.
Keep the change inside the requested scope. Conditional obligations:

Follow the repository's branch-naming convention; without one, prefixes such as `feature/`, `fix/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `docs/`, `chore/` are reasonable defaults. Use meaningful names and do not rename an existing user branch to satisfy a convention. One branch must not be checked out in multiple normal worktrees; keep each worktree focused on its branch's concern; before removing a worktree, verify its changes are committed or otherwise preserved, and never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.

Run `verify` before preparing a PR. A PR has a focused purpose without accidental unrelated changes; its description explains what changed, why, how it was verified, and compatibility/migration notes. Never claim checks that were not run.

- Keep implementation details non-public when they are not part of the project's public API; use `sealed` to communicate a deliberate "not for inheritance" design, not as a speculative JIT optimization.
- Do not reorganize an existing file merely to satisfy a preferred member ordering.
- Immutability where it represents the model naturally; controlled mutation where framework models or workflows are simpler with it.

When explicitly asked to modernize: preserve behavior, keep the change focused, prefer readability improvements, build and test afterwards, and do not mix architecture refactoring into syntax modernization.

The task is complete when the structure matches the requested scope, references respect the architecture, approved technology is used, no unnecessary projects or speculative directories exist, the backend builds, the frontend builds when present, relevant tests pass, the local Development configuration is usable, and no unrelated code was reorganized.

Review the final diff after all fixes. Check for accidental unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME markers, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved drift from `SPECIFICATION.md` or `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md`, stale code/tests/docs/config after a settings change, and behavior verified manually but never preserved as a test.
